signatureGenerator.title: Signature Generator
signatureGenerator.description: Draw or type your name to create a signature image, then save it as a trimmed transparent PNG, SVG or JPG. For e-contracts, PDFs and email — nothing is uploaded.

howItWorks.title: How it works
items: Pointer Events handle mouse, touch and stylus the same way, and the canvas disables touch-action so the page doesn't scroll while you draw.
Input points are joined with a Catmull-Rom spline converted to cubic Bézier curves, passing through every point without kinks.
Line width follows drawing speed (px/ms): slower is thicker, faster is thinner, smoothed to avoid jumps. Stylus pressure is used directly.
On export the signature is redrawn at 1–3x on a transparent canvas, trimmed to the ink using the alpha channel, and padded.
SVG export groups curves of equal width into single paths, so lines stay crisp at any size.

realWorld.title: Use it for
items: Adding a signature image to PDF contracts and consent forms (Acrobat Fill & Sign, macOS Preview)
Inserting a transparent PNG into Word or Hangul documents
Adding a handwritten signature to Gmail or Outlook email signatures
Signing quotes, statements and receipts
Uploading a ready-made signature to e-contract services that accept images

comparison.title: Comparing options
items: Draw — your own handwriting, the most natural. Touch or stylus gives much cleaner results than a mouse.
Type name — fast and consistent when drawing is hard, but anyone can produce the same look.
PNG vs SVG vs JPG — transparent PNG (2x) for documents, SVG for print and scaling, JPG where transparency isn't supported.
Signature image vs digital signature — an image is only the look of a signature; contracts that need identity verification require certificate-based e-signatures.

usage.title: How to Use
items: Draw your signature with mouse or touch on canvas
Adjust pen color and thickness
Transparent background for document overlay
Download as PNG or SVG format

tips.title: Tips
items: Transparent PNG at 2x works for most documents; use 3x or SVG for print or large sizes.
Blue ink makes an original signature easy to tell apart from a photocopy and is common for contracts.
Drawing with a mouse is hard — open this page on your phone and sign with your finger.
Copied signatures can be pasted directly into Word, Hangul, PowerPoint or email (browser support varies).
A signature image is not proof of identity. Use certificate-based e-signatures for important contracts.

whatIs.title: What is the signature generator?
whatIs.description: Create a signature image for e-contracts, PDFs and email. Draw with a mouse, finger or stylus and the stroke width follows your speed and pressure, or type your name and pick a Korean or English handwriting font. Exports are trimmed to the signature automatically so they drop straight into documents.

howToUse.title: How to use
items: 1. Choose Draw or Type name.
2. Sign in the white area (undo/redo supported, Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z), or type your name and pick a font.
3. Adjust ink color (black, blue, custom) and thickness, or font size, slant and spacing.
4. Check the document preview to see how it looks on a signature line.
5. Pick a format (PNG, JPG, SVG) and resolution (1x–3x), then download or copy. Save up to 5 signatures under My signatures.

items.q: Is a signature image legally binding?
items.a: An electronic signature can be valid if the signer's identity and intent can be verified, but an image alone makes that hard to prove. For contracts that require identity verification, use certificate-based e-signatures or an e-contract platform.

items.q: How do I add it to Word or a PDF?
items.a: In Word, insert the PNG as a picture and set wrapping to 'In front of text'. For PDFs, use Adobe Acrobat's Fill & Sign, macOS Preview's signature tool, or any PDF editor that supports images.
